---
title: "The Clo-Author Codex"
subtitle: "Codex-First Research Workflow for Empirical Social Science"
---

The Clo-Author is a Codex-first workflow for empirical social science research. It preserves the original clo-author ideas — structured planning, worker-critic review, journal-aware peer review, and quality gates — but moves the runtime into a home-local Codex plugin plus a lightweight project constitution inside each repository.

**Historical origin:** [Pedro Sant'Anna's claude-code-my-workflow](https://github.com/pedrohcgs/claude-code-my-workflow), reoriented for empirical research publication.

## Get Started in 5 Minutes

### Step 1: Prepare the local plugin

The recommended runtime is a home-local plugin:

- plugin root: `~/plugins/clo-author-codex`
- marketplace entry: `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`

The plugin carries the reusable parts of the workflow: skills, prompts, references, hooks, scripts, and template assets.

### Step 2: Clone or open a project

```bash
gh repo fork hugosantanna/clo-author --clone
cd clo-author
```

If you already have a repository, make sure it has `AGENTS.md`, `clo-author.toml`, and the standard research directories so the plugin can detect it automatically.

### Step 3: Open the repository in Codex

Once inside Codex, the plugin should detect the project and load the Clo-Author workflow through:

- `AGENTS.md`
- `clo-author.toml`
- the repository layout

### Step 4: Start with a skill or plain-language request

Examples:

- "Use `$discover` to build a literature review on health insurance and labor supply."
- "Use `$review` to run a methods-heavy review on `paper/main.tex`."
- "Use `$new-project` to initialize a new empirical project on municipal finance."

Natural language works too. The explicit skill names are useful when you want to steer Codex directly.

## What Happens Behind the Scenes

The Codex version keeps the same workflow logic:

- plan first for substantial work
- save artifacts to `quality_reports/`
- run worker-critic review by default
- route to referee-style review when needed
- verify before completion

The main difference is the runtime model. Instead of a Claude-only command stack, Codex uses:

- plugin skills
- prompt roles
- project detection hooks
- helper scripts for initialization, migration, logging, and review nudges

## Day 1 Checklist

- [ ] Ensure the home-local plugin is installed
- [ ] Open a repository with `AGENTS.md` and `clo-author.toml`
- [ ] Confirm Codex detects the project
- [ ] Start with `$discover`, `$review`, or `$new-project`
- [ ] Review the generated plan or artifact
- [ ] Let the worker-critic loop run before treating the result as final

That is the core loop. Everything else — prompts, references, hooks, and reports — supports that workflow.
